nodes.name: In situ FePc-GA synthesis
nodes.procedure: GO and FePc powders are uniformly dispersed in water through sonication forming acoustic cavitation that generates bubbles promoting penetration of water molecules into the solid and improving dispersion, forming a stable colloid. Due to the presence of many oxygen-containing functional groups such as hydroxyl, carboxyl, and epoxy groups on the surface of graphene oxide, these hydrophilic functional groups overcome van der Waals forces on the carbon skeleton itself under the strong electrostatic repulsion induced by the solvent. During the subsequent hydrothermal process, the oxygen functional groups on the surface of GO can be partly reduced and eliminated, increasing the π-conjugated structure of the reduced graphene oxide sheets (rGO). This allows them to form π-π conjugated stacking, making FePc and the rGO sheets closely bonding together. Finally, through freeze-drying, the solvent molecules in the hydrogel are converted into gas molecules, thereby in situ synthesizing a three-dimensional FePc-GA network structure material with high porosity, high specific surface area, and high compressibility.

unit_operations.name: Sonication
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: GO and FePc powders are uniformly dispersed in water through sonication forming acoustic cavitation that generates bubbles in the liquid, and the growth and collapse of these bubbles concentrate a large amount of energy inside the solution, promoting the penetration of water molecules into the solid. This improves the dispersion of the catalyst, ensuring that GO and FePc powders are uniformly dispersed in water, forming a stable colloid.

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal self-assembly
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: During the subsequent hydrothermal process, the oxygen functional groups on the surface of GO can be partly reduced and eliminated, increasing the π-conjugated structure of the reduced graphene oxide sheets (rGO). This allows them to form π-π conjugated stacking, making FePc and the rGO sheets closely bonding together.

unit_operations.name: Freeze drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Finally, through freeze-drying, the solvent molecules in the hydrogel are converted into gas molecules, thereby in situ synthesizing a three-dimensional FePc-GA network structure material.

nodes.procedure: FePc was combined with the hydrothermal GA to obtain GA-FePc, in which FePc can hardly couple with GA through π-π conjugated stacking.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows aggregated FePc on GA sheets for GA-FePc and uniform 2D planar layered structure with no large FePc aggregations for FePc-GA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a-c, for GA-FePc, aggregated FePc was observed on the GA sheets. ... In contrast, the morphology of FePc-GA, depicted in Figure 2d-g, shows ... uniform two-dimensional planar layered structure with no noticeable presence of large FePc aggregations.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-magnification TEM reveals aggregated FePc on GA sheets for GA-FePc; planar aggregated FePc coupled to ultrathin GA sheets through π-π stacking for FePc-GA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further TEM observation of the morphology and microstructure revealed that the planar aggregated FePc was coupled to the ultrathin GA sheets through π-π stacking.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping confirms presence of FePc coupled to graphene aerogel sheets in FePc-GA; shows distribution of Fe, N, O, and C elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, EDS mapping (Figure 2g) confirmed the presence of FePc coupled to graphene aerogel sheets. Figure 2h shows the distribution of Fe, N, O, and C elements with specific values detailed in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: GA has ID/IG = 1.02 indicating high graphitization; FePc-GA and GA-FePc have ID/IG = 1.05 and 1.04 respectively due to FePc coupling inducing defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra (Figures 3a and S5) display the intensity variations of the D band ... indicating changes in the defects and graphite phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: FePc-GA shows enhanced thermal stability with ~5 wt% loss at 100°C and stable mass loss between 300-600°C; FePc pyrolyzes completely at ~400°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To demonstrate the thermal stability of the materials, TGA tests were conducted (Figure 3b,c). Notably, the in situ synthesized FePc-GA exhibited enhanced thermal stability in air.

properties.description: FePc molecular structure with central Fe atom (blue/purple)

nodes.characterization_summary: DTG reveals weight change stages for FePc-GA: magnetite (Fe3O4) formation up to 400°C, conversion to Fe2O3 at 500°C, complete pyrolysis beyond 600°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Differential thermogravimetric analysis (DTG) (Figure 3c) further revealed the various stages of weight change during the process.

nodes.characterization_summary: FePc-GA and GA-FePc show sharp peak at 7.05° for FePc; FePc-GA FePc peaks weakened and shifted to lower angles due to π-π interaction; GA peaks at 25.4° (C 002) and 44.5° (C 101).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3d shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of all of the materials. Both FePc-GA and GA-FePc exhibit a sharp peak at 7.05°, indicating the presence of FePc.

properties.description: Scanning electron microscopy image showing porous microstructure

nodes.characterization_summary: FePc-GA shows N-Fe bond at 923 cm⁻¹, C-N at 1248 cm⁻¹, N-H at 1627 cm⁻¹ confirming FePc-GA composite formation; reduced OH intensity on GA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further investigate the chemical structure of the synthesized electrocatalysts, Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy (Figure 3e) ... FePc-GA exhibits a vibrational signal for the N-Fe bond at 923 cm⁻¹ within the fingerprint region.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show peak absorption at 663 nm attributed to electron delocalization effect in FePc.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The UV-Vis spectra of all samples (Figure 3f) display a peak absorption at 663 nm, attributed to the electron delocalization effect in FePc.
